behaviors: Read both original triggers and platform branches: absent/empty WORKSPACER_PARENT_PID disables watching, malformed text retains stdin EOF only, valid parent uses Unix signal0/EPERM liveness or one pinned Windows SYNCHRONIZE handle; first completed trigger shuts down standalone ownership.

Rust CLI preserves these decisions using cancellable nonblocking probes plus bounded reads; the embedded Backend never installs this CLI parent watcher or takes over host stdin/signals. Parent-handle RAII closes on cancellation instead of leaving a detached goroutine.

A dedicated Windows CLI parent-death runtime check is still needed for the final platform gate.

behaviors: Compared CreateJob/extended KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE/assignment/failure-close/lifetime semantics. Rust Job owns one spawned child and explicitly refuses the embedding process; closing the owned handle terminates assigned child and inherited descendants. This replaces the Go hub process-wide job, which would be unsafe to impose on an embedded GUI.

Existing actual Windows tests prove host-process refusal, assigned child exit and a descendant created after assignment dying when the job closes. Native installer/backend shutdown also passed on Windows; no cross-compilation-only claim.
intentionalChanges: Job ownership errors are propagated by owned launch helpers rather than merely logged while continuing unconfined. Non-Windows uses existing owned process-group cleanup rather than a dummy Confine no-op. This does not promise cleanup of arbitrary deliberately escaped Unix descendants.

All owned Windows launches now CREATE_SUSPENDED, assign the per-child kill-on-close job before user code, then resume the verified original initial thread. ConPTY uses the minimal portable-pty creation-flags patch. Actual std/Tokio/ConPTY immediate-fork regressions prove original descendant handles become signaled after cleanup without a stdin admission barrier. Failed assignment/resume fails closed; the host GUI is never assigned.
